Yelp launches new AI assistant to help consumers easily find and connect with service professionals | Yelp - Official Blog Skip to main content Toggle site navigation Yelp - Official Blog Blog News Businesses Community Life at Yelp Yelp.com Yelp for Business Search Yelp News Yelp launches new AI assistant to help consumers easily find and connect with service professionals Yelp’s Spring Release unveils new features that leverage LLMs to better connect consumers and pros, and bring Yelp content to third-party platforms; Yelp Guest manager enhancements improve operational efficiency for restaurants Craig Saldanha Chief Product Officer April 30, 2024 Share This In this Spring Release we’re introducing: Yelp Assistant, a new conversational AI feature that intelligently guides you through the process of finding the right pro for the job, transforming how you discover, connect with and hire service professionals. Yelp Fusion AI API, enabling third-party partners to integrate Yelp’s trusted content into their products to create natural language search experiences. Yelp Guest Manager enhancements that improve and streamline front-of-house operations, Waitlist and Kiosk updates to help guests get seated faster and more efficiently. As Yelp approaches 20 years of connecting you with great local businesses, we’re continuously innovating to enrich your experience, whether you’re planning your next home project or looking for the perfect dining spot. What began as a review site that millions of people relied on for finding great restaurants and other local experiences, has evolved into a powerful platform that helps you easily navigate the often complex task of finding and hiring service professionals. Today, many of our users rely on Yelp to find the right service pro for their needs — in the first quarter of 2024, consumer interest in home services businesses was up nearly 30% compared to Q1 2019. And now we’re leveraging AI to make that process even easier. After recently announcing a series of new discovery, contribution, services and AI-powered features earlier this year, today we’re unveiling our Spring Product Release with more than 15 new features and updates that will transform the Yelp experience. Our new AI-powered Yelp Assistant will revolutionize how you discover and connect with service pros. For partners, the new Yelp Fusion AI API will allow third-party platforms to create natural language search experiences powered by Yelp content. For restaurants, enhancements to Yelp Guest Manager will help them seat more diners by boosting front of house efficiency; and more. Yelp Assistant transforms how you discover and hire services professionals with conversational AI Whether you’re in need of quotes to repair your roof, looking to get your car detailed, or want to change up your hairstyle, Yelp Assistant, a new conversational AI feature, reinvents how you connect with and hire service professionals. Powered by large language models (LLMs), Yelp Assistant intelligently guides you through the process of finding the right pro for the job. It contextually understands your project or problem, engages in a professional-like dialogue with follow up questions, and then matches you with businesses that are qualified to help with your project. Unlike any other solution available today, Yelp Assistant is able to efficiently translate your problem and identify the right provider for your needs because the LLM is trained on Yelp’s vast and reliable dataset, including Request a Quote, business information, and more, in addition to LLMs from OpenAI. With its effective and precise matching capabilities, Yelp Assistant is delivering highly relevant, detailed leads to businesses, enabling them to more efficiently assess the project and get hired. Yelp Assistant is a new conversational AI feature that redefines the way consumers connect with businesses across thousands of service categories within home, local, auto, beauty, and more. Yelp Assistant not only helps you connect with pros who are suited for your project, but it also alleviates the guesswork on the type of specialists you may need, making hiring the right pros straightforward and stress-free. Once you let Yelp Assistant know what project or issue you’re looking to solve, it quickly springs into action with a personalized conversation to collect the necessary details a pro would need to evaluate your project. You have the option to either craft your own replies, choose from a selection of convenient one-click responses, or ask it a question to help further refine your response. After you review and approve the final project request, Yelp Assistant then creates and sends detailed project submissions to relevant service providers on your behalf, enabling businesses to better respond with accurate pricing and availability. Yelp Assistant can connect you with businesses across thousands of categories within home, local, auto, beauty, pet, real estate, professional, event planning, financial services, and more. It’s currently available on iOS from the ‘Projects’ tab and will roll out to Android later this summer.  In addition to Yelp Assistant, today we’re introducing other updates to help you connect with service pros. Yelp’s new Project Ideas, accessible through the ‘Projects’ tab, provide recommendations to help inspire your next home upgrade, alleviate decision paralysis, and make it easy to request quotes from service pros in your area. This summer, we’ll refine Project Ideas with predictive analysis to provide you with more personalized Project Ideas, recommendations and checklists. Plus, service pros will find business owner inbox enhancements that help them quickly respond to and secure jobs. New Saved Replies, currently available on iOS, allow business owners to effortlessly create and save response templates for common questions. They’ll also be able to stay more organized with updates that distinguish new leads from previously contacted messages, and new city location tags that easily identify the service area. Project Ideas help inspire your next endeavor, and new inbox enhancements help business owners quickly respond to and secure jobs. Yelp Fusion AI API brings natural language search to third-party partners Third-party partners can now integrate Yelp’s trusted content into their products to create conversational AI experiences with the new Yelp Fusion AI API. For years, Yelp Fusion has enabled consumers to access Yelp’s high quality information on local businesses in other places across the web, on mobile and in cars and homes. Our new LLM-powered partner solution, Yelp Fusion AI API, enables innovative user experiences using natural language search, even if partners have no previous AI products or experiences. Utilizing Yelp’s reliable local data and content — including business information, reviews and photos — the Yelp Fusion AI API enhances discovery on third-party platforms by enabling conversational queries like, “Find a vegan brunch place with a patio that’s open this Sunday at 10:00 a.m.,” or, “Recommend a good gym in Miami that has a swimming pool.” The AI will provide responses that are contextual to the conversation, sharing relevant businesses with detailed information, including Yelp ratings, review highlights , photos, business summaries , and more.  This new solution not only benefits partners by enabling conversational engagement using Yelp content, but it also reduces their need to acquire and manage data, ultimately making it easier and more efficient for their users to find great local businesses. The Yelp Fusion AI API represents a significant advancement in our mission to connect people with great local businesses, by opening new possibilities for these connections to be made seamlessly both on and off of Yelp. The Yelp Fusion AI API is currently available for partners to integrate into their platform, and  non-partners can test out the AI API with 30-day access or contact us to learn more. Today, the Yelp Fusion AI API supports single-turn questions and responses, with multi-turn conversations coming later this year. The Yelp Fusion AI API helps partners integrate natural language search experiences into their own platforms. Enhancing the Restaurant Experience with Yelp Guest Manager Yelp Guest Manager , our comprehensive front-of-house solution, gives more than 11,000 restaurants access to the largest diner network.* Now, with new features that streamline front-of-house operations, enhance analytics for restaurant owners, and improve Yelp Waitlist and Kiosk, restaurants can boost efficiency, seat more diners, and improve guest experiences. Revamped Yelp Guest Manager provides hosts with smarter insights We’re introducing a new suite of features for Yelp Guest Manager that provide hosts with a deeper understanding of their guests’ needs, enabling more effective staff utilization, better preparedness for upcoming shifts, and streamlined operations. Cover Flow makes it even easier to plan for and manage the dinner rush by helping hosts better optimize server sections and table assignments, and monitor table status in real time. Party Highlights empower staff to create more personalized and attentive guest experiences, while Shift Notes streamline front of house communication by centralizing information for staff. Plus, credit card holds for in-house reservations just got easier with automated SMS confirmations sent to guests, eliminating the need for hosts to manually enter credit card information. New analytics drive operational efficiency for restaurant owners It’s not just hosts getting a revamped Yelp Guest Manager experience, business owners will also find new table usage analytic s, user permissions functionality, online reservation management features, and traffic analytics in their Yelp business owner account. The new analytics dashboard displays a holistic view of table states and usage, including seat delay and average table turn time, enabling restaurant owners to better find efficiencies and increase diners seated. New user permissions, rolling out in the coming weeks, provide restaurant owners and general managers with more precise control over staff access to Yelp Guest Manager features, getting the right tools into the right hands. With online reservation management, restaurants can now create reservations and assign tables without having to use the host app. These new updates are available in the Yelp Guest Manager business owner account s on desktop. And in the coming months, restaurant owners will have access to new traffic attribution analytics that detail valuable cover and booking trends. New Waitlist updates improve wait time accuracy and diner communication Yelp Waitlist has made it easier than ever for diners to join the waitlist at their favorite restaurants from anywhere, while freeing up host time to focus on other important front-of-house operations. Wait time accuracy continues to improve with AI through our use of neural networks to help diners better plan their restaurant outings. In addition to more accurate wait times, new text message place-in-line updates, such as if the line is moving faster or slower than anticipated, mean there’s no need for diners to keep an eye on the app or ask when they’ll be seated. Soon, diners will also receive texts to check out popular dishes before they’re seated. Hosts can automate updates or send them manually, simplifying diner communication and helping them seat guests faster, reducing table turn times. Redesigned Yelp Kiosk enhances the diner check in experience Yelp Kiosk just got a new look. This newly redesigned experience makes it easier to join the waitlist and check yourself in when you’re at the restaurant, streamlining the process for diners while allowing the host to manage other front-of-house operations. Shift Notes (left), Table Usage Analytics (center) and new text message place-in-line updates (right) streamline front-of-house operations, boost efficiency and improve communication amongst staff and guests. Our mission to connect people with great local businesses has never been more relevant. The introduction of Yelp Assistant and the enhancements across our platform are testaments to our ongoing commitment to innovation and delighting our users. By continually evolving and adapting to the needs of our community, Yelp is setting the stage for a future where every interaction is smarter, more intuitive, and tailored to meet the dynamic needs of consumers and businesses. Yelp introduces Request a Quote for Brands and unveils a series of new updates for national advertisers | Yelp - Official Blog Skip to main content Toggle site navigation Yelp - Official Blog Blog News Businesses Community Life at Yelp Yelp.com Yelp for Business Search Yelp News Yelp introduces Request a Quote for Brands and unveils a series of new updates for national advertisers Yelp’s Summer Ad Release highlights new features and updates for multi-location businesses that enable service pros to drive and manage more leads, help advertisers better reach their audiences on and off Yelp, and enhance their ability to analyze any conversion from lead to transaction Craig Saldanha Chief Product Officer July 23, 2024 Share This In this Summer Ad Release we’re introducing: A suite of features to help multi-location services businesses generate and manage high-intent leads — including Request a Quote for Brands, Yelp Guaranteed, Verified License, and Portfolio.  New and expanded ad formats and measurement tools for national advertisers, including enhancements to Spotlight video ads, the expansion of Yelp Audiences for audio platforms, and a new conversion API that improves advertiser measurement. As Yelp celebrates its 20th anniversary, our mission to connect people with great businesses remains at the forefront of everything we do. Our commitment to product innovation is designed to meet the diverse needs of all our users, including consumers and businesses across categories and sizes. Since April 2023, we’ve introduced more than 75 new features and updates to help consumers find the right businesses for their needs, and help businesses successfully attract new customers.   Today, we are delivering on our commitment to drive more value to national services businesses and advertisers across categories with a series of new features and updates. With Request a Quote for Brands, enterprise services businesses will be able to leverage the power of Request a Quote, Yelp Guaranteed, and more, to simplify lead generation and management across multiple locations and give consumers peace of mind when hiring service providers. New video and audio ad formats offer innovative ways for both advertisers to reach audiences on and off Yelp, while also helping them future-proof their measurement strategies. People frequently come to Yelp to engage with national brands, and we’re excited to introduce new features that help them achieve their business and advertising goals. Request a Quote for Brands helps national services businesses seamlessly drive and manage leads Millions of people come to Yelp to connect with pros, whether they are in search of a new landscaper, need to repair a dent in their car, or want to find a new hairdresser for a special occasion. As our fastest-growing category, services businesses have found notable success on Yelp as we’ve prioritized building innovative features that help them reach and connect with customers. Now, for the first time, we’re expanding many of these features, including Request a Quote , Yelp Guaranteed , Portfolio , and Verified License , to brands and multi-location businesses. R equest a Quote for Brands allows Yelp users to find service pros at multi-location businesses; Request a Quote, Yelp Guaranteed, Portfolio, and Verified License are now available for brands. Request a Quote for Brands and the new Leads API unlock enhanced lead generation and management  First introduced in 2016, Request a Quote, which has helped local businesses generate leads and connect with customers, is now available for multi-location brands. The new Request a Quote for Brands will help national services businesses reach more high-intent consumers, while the new Leads API will enable them to manage leads across all their locations seamlessly within their existing customer management tools — eliminating the need to manually manage leads from multiple Yelp pages. Whether a consumer connects with pros through Request a Quote or through our AI-powered Yelp Assistant , multi-location businesses using the Leads API will be able to receive and manage these leads easier than ever. This means more leads delivered directly to businesses and more options for consumers looking to hire service providers. Request a Quote for Brands is now available for multi-location businesses across most services categories. National services businesses like Roadway Moving are already seeing strong results from an early test. “As we aim to attract more potential customers interested in moving services, Request a Quote has become an important part of our lead generation strategy,” said Ross Sapir, president of Roadway Moving. “Yelp’s Leads API enhances our ability to manage leads from Yelp by enabling direct communication with our customers across multiple locations and managing these relationships in real time. This streamlined process makes it easier for our sales team to use, and ultimately drives more business.” Yelp Guaranteed boosts customer confidence in hiring multi-location businesses As a part of the Request a Quote for Brands suite of features, we’re also extending the Yelp Guaranteed customer satisfaction program to support eligible projects with national services businesses that advertise and activate Request a Quote in popular categories. When a customer hires a business for a Yelp Guaranteed project through Request a Quote, they are automatically covered for up to $2,500 if something goes wrong with their project. This guarantee increases customer confidence, helping businesses convert more leads into jobs. Yelp Guaranteed is available across many popular services categories, such as contractors , HVAC , plumbers , and movers , with more categories available in the coming months. Verified License and Portfolio boost customer trust and showcase business expertise for national services businesses We are rolling out our Verified License program and Portfolio products to national services businesses. Launched in 2019 , Verified License makes it easy to find businesses with valid trade licenses, helping consumers make confident decisions when choosing a business for their project. Portfolio allows businesses to showcase their specialties through a photo collection of projects, allowing potential customers to assess the quality of work and decide if the business is the right fit for their upcoming project. Verified License and Portfolio are available to eligible national services businesses that enable Request a Quote. Expanded ad formats and new measurement tools drive more value to national advertisers We first introduced ad products for multi-location advertisers in 2019 and have continued to innovate with new products and features that help this segment of businesses engage with our high-intent audience. Today, we’re announcing several updates for these advertisers, including enhancements to Spotlight Ads to enable brands to surface video ads in new ways across the Yelp platform; an expansion of Yelp Audiences to audio platforms and connected TV providers; and a new conversion API that will help advertisers more effectively measure their ads. More Spotlight Ad placements extend advertiser reach on Yelp Originally launched in 2022, Spotlight Ads have provided national businesses with an impactful way to reach Yelp’s users by displaying a video or photo ad unit on the home feed. Today, we’re expanding Spotlight Ads video placements to also appear among the photos on Yelp business pages, a highly trafficked destination, helping both location and non-location-based advertisers reach even more consumers across the platform. In early tests, brands like Prime Video and Virgin Voyages used Spotlight Ads to increase awareness and consideration intent among Yelp’s audiences. Yelp Audiences brings off-platform ads to audio platforms and connected TV Yelp Audiences , our enterprise solution that helps brands reach Yelp’s high-intent audiences on other websites and platforms based on Yelp search activity, now allows advertisers to reach even more of Yelp’s high-intent audience on connected TV (CTV) and audio platforms. Advertisers will now be able to target audio ads to Yelp users when they’re streaming music and listening to podcasts across Spotify, Pandora, SiriusXM, iHeart, and more. We’ve also made our CTV offering more cost-effective for brands while maintaining our high standard of premium inventory sources, including platforms like Hulu, Disney+, and Paramount+. These improvements have resulted in more brands using CTV through Yelp Audiences in 2024 to date than in all of 2023. To leverage Yelp Audiences , advertisers provide creative assets and Yelp delivers the ads on premium websites, mobile apps, and video and audio streaming services, based on the user’s search intent while on Yelp. New conversion API helps advertisers measure success without cookies The new conversion API (CAPI) offers brand advertisers an even more accurate way to measure the value of Yelp Ads while also future-proofing their measurement strategy. CAPI allows brands to analyze any conversion from lead to transaction, measuring what matters most for them without relying on cookie signals, whether conversions happen online, offline, or in-app.  In early testing, CAPI is already driving significant value for advertisers. “When we measure our return on ad spend from a last-click perspective, we’re about 2x to 4x on Yelp,” said Paul Baumgarthuber, chief marketing officer at LaserAway . “When we matched the data to understand how Yelp Ads influences our customers, we’re at about 8x return on ad spend using Yelp’s conversion API product.” CAPI is now available to any brand advertiser at no additional cost. Our commitment to connecting people with great local businesses continues to be the north star guiding our product innovation. By expanding our offerings for national services providers, we are not only helping businesses manage and drive leads more effectively, but also providing consumers with more options so they can be confident in their choices. New products and offerings for national brands will give these advertisers more options to reach our audiences.  As we continue to adapt and innovate, Yelp is poised to support the dynamic needs of national businesses, setting the stage for a future where every interaction is more intuitive and valuable. Stay tuned for more exciting developments as we continue to enhance our platform and services. If you’re a multi-location business or brand interested in learning more about advertising on Yelp, visit Yelp for Brands . Academic research finds Yelp's content moderation practices mitigate misinformation and build consumer trust | Yelp - Official Blog Skip to main content Toggle site navigation Yelp - Official Blog Blog News Businesses Community Life at Yelp Yelp.com Yelp for Business Search Yelp News Academic research finds Yelp’s content moderation practices mitigate misinformation and build consumer trust Aaron Schur General Counsel September 20, 2023 Share This The Journal of Marketing Research recently published a study that evaluates how online review platforms can effectively build trust with consumers.* This independent research (not funded by Yelp or any of the other platforms evaluated) identifies five key mechanisms that review platforms can implement to curb less trustworthy content and build trust with consumers: monitoring (evaluating reviews for authenticity), exposure (exposing firms propagating fake reviews), community building (enabling consumer and reviewer interactions), status endowment (recognizing credible and helpful reviewers), and identity disclosure (having reviewers share identifying details such as a real name). After examining 25 review platforms, the study found that Yelp is one of two platforms that applies all five mechanisms and as the research states, has become a “guardian of trust” for review information. The research evaluated many of the mechanisms Yelp has long used, most going back to the beginnings of our company, to surface reliable information, including our automated recommendation software , human moderation efforts , Consumer Alerts program , the Yelp Elite Squad , and other community building features of the platform. Our research indicated Yelp as a leader in building consumer trust through adoption of trust building practices. Those findings were confirmed further as we showed the results to Yelp staff and saw their commitment to improving trust on their platform and in their industry at large. Ben B. Beck, PhD MBA, Brigham Young University Yelp leverages automated and human moderation practices  The study finds that “monitoring” is the most impactful practice used to build trust with consumers, as well as the most likely to be implemented (52% of platforms adopted monitoring), defined by the researchers as when a platform “communicates it verifies the authenticity of reviews (manually as well as via a proprietary algorithm).” With hundreds of millions of reviews contributed to Yelp since our inception, we leverage our automated recommendation software to help surface helpful and reliable content to consumers. The software evaluates reviews based on hundreds of signals of quality, reliability, and user activity on Yelp. For example, the software is programmed to catch unfairly biased reviews, reviews likely coming from online review exchange groups, and more. Our stance is quality over quantity when it comes to reviews. As a result, we currently only recommend about 74% of the reviews that have been submitted on our platform and only recommended reviews are factored into a business’s overall star rating.  We also rely on our user community of consumers and businesses to help report suspicious content to Yelp when they believe it may violate our policies. Every report is reviewed by our moderators and we routinely act on tips surrounding potential deceptive behaviors. In 2022, Yelp’s content moderation team removed more than 206,700 reported reviews. Beyond reports from our users, we also proactively moderate content on the platform by conducting regular internal investigations, as well as removing reviews and user accounts we determine to be deceptive. Yelp’s Consumer Alerts warns consumers of suspicious behavior  The study observed if review platforms publicly expose generators of fake reviews. In addition to monitoring, exposure was found to be one of the most impactful mechanisms in building consumer trust. That said, only 24% of all the review platforms evaluated implemented practices to expose those selling reviews, demonstrating that while it may be the most effective trust building practice, it’s also the toughest to execute.  Yelp issues a variety of Consumer Alerts that help raise awareness among consumers of deceptive practices that they might not otherwise know about, allowing people to make better informed spending decisions. For example, our Compensated Activity Alerts are placed on business pages when we receive evidence that someone has offered cash or other incentives in exchange for a review and our Suspicious Review Activity Alerts are placed on business pages to warn consumers when we detect a large number of reviews coming from a single IP address, or reviews from users who may be connected to a group that coordinates incentivised fake reviews.  When we do issue an alert, a warning message is displayed over the reviews of that business’s Yelp page informing consumers about the violation of our policies with a link to view evidence we collected when available. This evidence can provide more details for consumers about the behavior we are warning them about, including who is responsible for it. For more than a decade Yelp has issued Consumer Alerts on business pages to warn consumers of potentially unreliable and deceptive behavior, whereas other sites may not provide equivalent information or even acknowledge the existence of attempts to deceive consumers on their platforms. …Exposing deviant selling firms signals that the platform is both willing and capable to police fake reviews, thus building platform trust… From Guardians of Trust: How Review Platforms Can Fight Fakery and Build Consumer Trust Yelp Elite badges distinguish our most active and helpful users  Status endowment refers to when a review platform “awards a badge of credibility to reviewers who are evaluated by consumers as particularly helpful.” The study found that credibility badges reinforce reviewer trustworthiness since they are earned over longer periods of time by a platform’s most consistent users, making it more challenging for nefarious users to game the system to conduct deceptive behaviors. Yelp’s status endowment mechanism, as evaluated in this study, is the Yelp Elite Squad , which was founded in 2005 to recognize users who consistently contribute quality content. Elites are typically locals who are eager to discover new businesses in their area and are passionate about sharing their discoveries with others. Yelp users can nominate themselves to join the Yelp Elite Squad or users can nominate other community members they think are a great representation of the Yelp community. We have systems in place to evaluate nominees and determine if they are a good fit for the Yelp Elite Squad, with one of the goals being to limit membership to users who have not engaged in suspicious activity on our platform. Yelp fosters community-building among users Another attribute that helps review platforms build consumer trust is community building, or when a platform “provides forums where consumers can interact with reviews and ask about their experiences.” A focus on community-building helps reduce incentives for bad actors to manipulate content because reviewers are often expected to provide high-quality and in-depth insights. Building our local communities both on and off the Yelp platform has been central to Yelp’s mission. We provide ways for our users to follow one another , react to reviews , send direct messages to other reviewers, and publicly answer people’s questions about a business through our Ask the Community section on business pages.  We also have numerous mechanisms in place that enable businesses to engage with the Yelp community. We encourage business owners to claim their Yelp page for free, post photos, and update their business information, as well as publish public responses to reviews, which are displayed next to the original review content. Yelp Elites are required to use their real name and photo The study found that identity disclosure – which refers to the practice of requiring “reviewers to share their true full name, city and state, and recent picture” -– creates an added layer of trustworthiness as consumers process review information. While the study found identity disclosure is helpful in building trust, if a platform applies exposure, community building and status endowment these mechanisms supersede the need for identity disclosure, which can raise privacy and free speech concerns. While it is not a requirement for Yelp users to use their real names on our platform, members of the Yelp Elite Squad are required to use their real names and a photo of themselves. Generally, Yelp allows reviewers to use a pseudonym, and defends their right to do so , which they might do if they’d like to leave a review on a sensitive subject matter (e.g., divorce lawyers, plastic surgeons, medical services, etc.) or want to avoid being stereotyped, having their opinion attributed to their employer or for other reasons. That said, we facilitate authentic content from the start of the user experience by encouraging users to complete public profiles and share information about themselves with our community. Yelp exists to connect people with great local businesses by giving them access to reliable and useful information. As part of this, we believe our users’ experiences on Yelp, from account creation, to reading reviews, to understanding how we moderate content, is critical to fostering trust in our platform. The processes we have in place aim to protect content integrity on Yelp and to provide users with the most helpful and reliable information, as well as provide a more level playing field for businesses that aren’t seeking to unfairly gain advantages over competitors through deceptive conduct. Read the full study in the Journal of Marketing Research: Guardians of Trust: How Review Platforms Can Fight Fakery and Build Consumer Trust *The findings presented in this article stem from an independent study. This research project is the result of a collaboration between Ben B. Beck, Assistant Professor of Marketing at Brigham Young University, Stefan Wuyts, Professor of Marketing at The Pennsylvania State University, and Sandy Jap, the Sarah Beth Brown Professor of Marketing at Emory University. The research was started as part of the dissertation of Ben B. Beck while he was at Penn State. Yelp publishes an index of Compensated and Suspicious Activity Consumer Alerts recipients and releases survey findings on what makes reviews trustworthy | Yelp - Official Blog Skip to main content Toggle site navigation Yelp - Official Blog Blog News Businesses Community Life at Yelp Yelp.com Yelp for Business Search Yelp News Yelp publishes an index of Compensated and Suspicious Activity Consumer Alerts recipients and releases survey findings on what makes reviews trustworthy Noorie Malik VP of User Operations September 20, 2023 Share This In a world where access to information can feel endless, online reviews have changed how we shop, dine and make important spending decisions. However, the reliability of information on the web is often questionable. As new rules are being proposed to create civil penalties for fake reviews and testimonials, it’s imperative for platforms to take steps to stem such deceptive content and maintain consumer trust in online reviews. A new survey commissioned by Yelp and conducted by Material , polling 2,000 Americans,  found that consumers are doing their due diligence before patronizing a business.* Nine out of ten respondents (93%) say they read online reviews to inform their purchasing decisions. The survey, announced today by Yelp, also found that a majority of respondents (76%) said they read more online reviews now than they ever have before and that it’s rare for them to visit an unfamiliar business without checking online reviews first (70%). These findings demonstrate how important it is to mitigate deceptive information — something Yelp has prioritized since its inception by investing significantly in technology and human moderation to protect the quality and integrity of content on the platform. In fact, a new study published in the Journal of Marketing Research found that Yelp’s content moderation practices are effective at mitigating misinformation and building consumer trust.  As a part of our commitment to protecting content integrity and preventing bad actors from gaming the system, along with the survey findings, today, we’re releasing a new index that regularly lists the latest Compensated Activity Alerts and Suspicious Review Activity Alerts we have placed on Yelp business pages, as well as historical recipients. Yelp displays the latest Compensated and Suspicious Review Activity Alerts As the online review landscape has grown, so has the potential for deceptive behavior by bad actors. One of the mechanisms we use to mitigate misinformation is our Consumer Alerts program . As a part of this program, we proactively investigate attempts to manipulate a business’s ratings and reviews, and may place an alert on a business page to warn people when we discover suspicious or misleading review activity. In fact, 85% of survey respondents say they want online review sites to tell them if the sites have reason to believe a business has ever received incentivized reviews.  Today, we’re introducing a new index on Yelp’s Trust & Safety site of the latest Compensated Activity Alerts and Suspicious Review Activity Alerts we have placed on business pages. Since 2012, Yelp has placed more than 4,900 Compensated Activity and Suspicious Review Activity Alerts on U.S. business pages. Compensated Activity Alerts indicate that we’ve caught someone offering payment in the form of cash, discounts, gift certificates or other incentives in exchange for writing, changing, preventing or removing reviews.  Suspicious Review Activity Alerts warn that we’ve detected a large number of positive reviews coming from a single IP address, or reviews from users who may be connected to a group that coordinates incentivized reviews.  Yelp strictly prohibits incentivizing or offering payment for reviews, as this behavior misleads consumers, artificially inflates ratings and is unfair to businesses who rightfully earn their great reputations on Yelp. If Yelp discovers a user is writing (or removing) reviews for compensation, our practice is to remove their reviews and close their account.  The Material survey findings show that offering payment for reviews erodes consumer trust as 68% of respondents indicated they would no longer visit a business if they learned a business received incentivized reviews. Now, in addition to displaying these alerts directly on a business’s Yelp page, Yelp is making it easy for consumers and regulators to identify businesses that we’ve detected have participated in suspicious or deceptive review activity with this new index. Yelp is also showing information about historical alerts, on trust.yelp.com/consumer-alerts/all . Relatedly, the Journal of Marketing Research also evaluated how online review platforms can effectively build trust with consumers, finding that publicly exposing businesses that solicit fake reviews is one of the hardest strategies for review platforms to implement. Only 24% of the 25 review platforms evaluated in the study implement this mechanism, including Yelp.  Consumers don’t trust solicited reviews and don’t want to be asked to leave a review Consumers feel pressure to positively inflate their rating when asked to leave a review compared to someone who was intrinsically motivated to write a review on their own. In fact, 65% of survey respondents who read reviews admitted they would write a more positive review than originally intended if a business asked them to leave a review, and 61% admitted they would provide a better star rating.  One of the policies that differentiates Yelp from other platforms is that we firmly prohibit solicited reviews, which our automated recommendation software is engineered to detect. Review solicitation leads to biased reviews and ratings, which are less helpful to consumers and give an unfair advantage to businesses with the time and marketing resources to ask a lot of customers for reviews or pay for reputation management services. While more than half of survey respondents (54%) say they wouldn’t trust reviews of businesses that ask customers to leave a review, 68% of respondents admitted they’ve been asked by a local business to leave them a review in the past. Consumers prioritize review transparency, and have picked up new ways to verify the reviews they see Savvy consumers look to trusted sources when it comes to online reviews, with many respondents (64%) that feel online reviews can be as trustworthy and helpful as personal referrals from their own friends and family. Most are looking for signs of trustworthiness like whether a reviewer frequently visits the type of business they’re evaluating (88%) or if the reviewer has written other reliable reviews in the past (78%). Nearly three-fourths of respondents (72%) trust the reviews of a review site’s power users over other reviewers. People also don’t think star ratings alone tell the whole story. More than 4 in 5 respondents (83%) say they’re more likely to trust a written review over just a star rating with no review text. On Yelp, review text must always accompany a star rating — without it there wouldn’t be enough information to help consumers make a purchasing decision, or feedback to help businesses improve their customer experience. In fact, the average length of recommended reviews contributed to Yelp was 471 characters as of December 31, 2022. Consumers go to review platforms for more than just ratings and reviews  People tend to rely on review platforms for more than just the star ratings and reviews — instead, they’re often gathering helpful details about the local businesses near them. For example, people say they rely on review platforms to view a menu (55%), confirm operating hours (54%), and check the address (54%), among other things. Only 17% of respondents say they visit review platforms solely for their reviews. In a crowded online marketplace, how are local businesses winning over potential customers?  Responding to reviews has been a proven way for businesses to earn the trust of current and potential customers. In fact, 86% of respondents say they’re more likely to look past a business’s critical reviews if they demonstrate their commitment to customer service by responding and adequately addressing the issue. Additionally, being an engaged business owner on review platforms helps to increase their review contributions. Most respondents who read reviews (70%) say they’re more likely to write a review for a business if they see the business owner responds to reviews. For nearly two decades, Yelp has prioritized maintaining the integrity and quality of the content on our platform. Academics , economists , industry experts , the media , and regulators have all acknowledged that Yelp is one of the most aggressive and successful at identifying and weeding out unreliable reviews. To learn about all the ways Yelp maintains the integrity and quality of our content, visit trust.yelp.com . *Material Survey 2023. This survey was fielded by Material among 2,000 people aged 18+ in the United States. The survey was conducted online during August 2023 and has a margin of error of +/- 2%.  Results of any sample are subject to sampling variation. The magnitude of the variation is measurable and is affected by the number of interviews and the level of the percentages expressing the results. September 13, 2023 Share This Update: This blog post has been updated to reflect FTC Economist Devesh Raval’s revised study, which was republished on May 23, 2024. Key Findings From “ Do Bad Businesses Get Good Reviews? Evidence Across Several Online Review Platforms ” For average business ratings, Yelp has a more uniform distribution between one and five stars, whereas Google, Facebook, and HomeAdvisor have skewed rating distributions that disproportionately favor higher star ratings. Reviews that contain 501 to 1,000 characters made up about 28% of Yelp reviews, compared to only 6% of Google reviews. In fact, 50% of Google’s reviews contain less than 100 characters — 32% of these so-called “reviews” contain no text at all. For suspicious businesses with a large number of consumer complaints and a low letter grade from the Better Business Bureau (BBB), businesses on Google had a significantly higher and favorable average star rating (3.5 stars) compared to Yelp (2.4 stars). This week, trial began in a case brought by the Justice Department, joined by dozens of states, against Google over its anticompetitive conduct in the online search industry. One of Google’s primary arguments to defend its dominant position is that its features are better for consumers, but when it comes to local business information like consumer reviews this is plainly not the case. Illustrating this, U.S. Federal Trade Commission (FTC) Economist Devesh Raval, recently released a study that supports arguments against Google’s anticompetitive self-preferencing conduct. Raval examined how local business reviews for generalist platforms, such as Google and Facebook,compare with specialized platforms like Yelp, HomeAdvisor, and the Better Business Bureau (BBB). The study’s findings support antitrust concerns that Google’s behavior harms consumers by prioritizing their own lower-quality features over competitor content with higher quality. Through Raval’s analyses, he found that Google, Facebook, and HomeAdvisor exhibit signs of rating inflation, even for lower-quality businesses that have received a poor letter grade from the BBB or had numerous consumer complaints filed against them. The study also finds that Yelp’s content policies, and trust and safety practices help mitigate the impact of lower quality or potentially fake reviews. Average business ratings on Yelp have a more uniform distribution than other platforms By evaluating a sample of nearly 135,000 businesses across all five platforms, the study found that average business ratings on Yelp are “much more uniform across the rating distribution” — about 32% of businesses are above four stars, 58% are between two and four stars, and 10% are below two stars. Google, Facebook, and HomeAdvisor have rating distributions that heavily skews toward higher star ratings. The percentage of businesses with at least four star ratings on each platform were 59% on Google, 79% on Facebook, and 96% on HomeAdvisor. Only 4% of businesses on Google and 2% of businesses on Facebook had an average rating below two stars. The study likens this to the Lake Wobegon effect , or a tendency to believe that the businesses listed on the respective platforms are all above average. Figure 1 from Do Bad Businesses Get Good Reviews? Evidence Across Several Online Review Platforms (page 16) Low-quality businesses have higher ratings on Google than Yelp The study categorizes the quality of a business based on the number of complaints filed with various consumer protection related organizations (such as the BBB or the FTC) and the letter grade a business receives from the BBB. High-quality tier: businesses with almost no complaints and almost all receive A+ grades from the BBB (27% of businesses in the sample) Medium-quality tier: businesses with complaints and grades in between A+ and F from the BBB (63% of businesses) Low-quality tier: businesses with a large number of complaints and more likely to receive a F grade from the BBB (10% of businesses) A low quality business on Google has about the same average rating as a medium quality business on Yelp or a high quality business on the BBB’s platform. Raval found that both low- and high-quality businesses have higher ratings on Google, Facebook, and HomeAdvisor compared to the BBB and Yelp. The average business ratings on Google, Facebook, and HomeAdvisor only see a slight decrease as business quality falls, whereas Yelp and the BBB see significant decreases. Google and Facebook both fell by 0.9 stars from high-quality to low-quality businesses, and HomeAdvisor fell by 0.5 stars. Additionally, to confirm if the slight decrease in average business ratings between high-quality and low-quality businesses may be due to the volume of Google reviews with less than 100 characters, Raval removed these reviews from his sample and still found a similar pattern between high-quality and low-quality businesses (both average ratings decreased). Raval concludes that, “A platform that spends less effort on reducing fake reviews is likely to have inflated reviews for low quality businesses.” Yelp takes extensive measures to mitigate against misinformation on our platform. Over the years, industry experts , the media , and regulators have shown that Yelp is one of the most aggressive and successful at identifying and weeding out unreliable reviews. Figure 3 from DDo Bad Businesses Get Good Reviews? Evidence Across Several Online Review Platforms (page 24) Google tends to have many lower quality reviews One differentiator between Yelp and other review platforms is that Yelp has always required review text to accompany ratings. Google allows users to leave a star rating with no review text, which the study found made up 32% of Google’s reviews and saw an overwhelmingly positive average of 4.3 stars. The study also revealed that 50% of Google reviews were 100 characters or less, compared to only 2% of Yelp reviews. Relatedly, a SOCi research report found that Google reviews with text have fallen 28% between January 2015 and July 2022, as bare ratings lacking context made up more of their local business content. Given the ease of leaving a star rating with no text on Google, bad actors have been able to weaponize Google ratings in an extortion scheme targeting numerous restaurants in major cities in 2022. In a Yelp-commissioned survey conducted by Material , 85% of respondents who read reviews say they’re more likely to trust a written review over just a star rating with no review text.* Raval’s study also found that 28% of Yelp reviews were between 501 and 1,000 characters, compared to only 6% of Google reviews. While Yelp and Google reviews with more than 1,000 characters both had an average rating of 2.5 stars, these longer reviews made up 18% of Yelp’s sample and only 2% of Google’s sample. The study highlights the value of requiring review text, stating, “Requiring a reviewer to write text imposes greater costs on reviewers, which might reduce the quantity of reviews but increase their quality.” Figure 5 from Do Bad Businesses Get Good Reviews? Evidence Across Several Online Review Platforms (page 32) The Material survey also found that 77% of respondents said they are reading more online reviews now than they ever have before, and 72% said it’s rare for them to visit an unfamiliar business without checking online reviews first.* This is why the quality and reliability of reviews has long been a top priority for Yelp. The trust consumers have in the ratings and reviews on Yelp is why we invest in significant measures to protect the integrity of content on our platform, including our automated recommendation software , reporting by Yelp’s community of business owners and users, human moderation , and our Consumer Alerts program. With average ratings of businesses on Google heavily skewed towards four or five stars, people may unwittingly be driven to businesses with numerous consumer complaints and F ratings from the BBB. As Raval puts it, “Google and Facebook are dominant platforms in search and social media markets; reviews are a small part of their business.” Generalist platforms like Google are able to leverage their monopoly distribution to steer consumers looking for a business on Google Search or Google Maps to their own business reviews, creating less incentive for them to take serious steps in reigning in the growing issue of fake reviews. Learn more in FTC Economist Devesh Raval’s full study: Do Bad Businesses Get Good Reviews? Evidence Across Several Online Review Platforms * Material Survey 2022. This survey was fielded by Material among 2,000 people aged 18+ in the United States. The survey was conducted online during the period of August and September 2022 and has a margin of error of +/- 2%.  Results of any sample are subject to sampling variation. The magnitude of the variation is measurable and is affected by the number of interviews and the level of the percentages expressing the results. 2024 Yelp Foundation Year in Review | Yelp - Official Blog Skip to main content Toggle site navigation Yelp - Official Blog Blog News Businesses Community Life at Yelp Yelp.com Yelp for Business Search Yelp News 2024 Yelp Foundation Year in Review Miriam Warren Chairperson of the Yelp Foundation December 9, 2024 Share This Since its inception in 2011, the Yelp Foundation has donated over $7 million to a diverse array of nonprofit organizations. The types of organizations we’ve funded have evolved over the years, but our mission remains steadfast: to support nonprofits that align with the Yelp Foundation’s mission and make a positive impact in communities where Yelp employees live and work. In parallel with Yelp’s commitment to being a fully remote employer in 2021 and its increasingly global workforce, the Yelp Foundation has significantly expanded its scope of nonprofit consideration in the past three years.  Our funding strategy and approach to selecting and supporting causes are based in trust; all grants made by the Yelp Foundation to nonprofit organizations are unrestricted. Unrestricted funding allows grantees to use the funds however they see fit. Charities can pay their employees, pay their electricity bills, or use them for direct programmatic costs. We trust that the organizations know more about the distribution of their resources than we do. We believe in their missions and want them to have the flexibility to accomplish their mission-driven work.  In our ongoing commitment to trust-based giving, the Yelp Foundation is thrilled to embark on new partnerships with organizations in the trades sector—an area we have not previously funded. Yelp is renowned for connecting people with great local businesses—whether they are looking for a delicious slice of pizza, a great avocado toast, or an up-and-coming ramen joint. Yelp can also help consumers find a plumber, an electrician, or an auto mechanic with the skills and tools they need most. As Yelp has directed its focus toward facilitating more seamless transactions between consumers and services pros , we’ve recognized a growing challenge: the skilled trades are facing a significant labor shortage . This shortage is exacerbated by stigmas associated with vocational training and a disproportionately aging workforce , with insufficient younger individuals entering these fields. Women, particularly women of color , are notably underrepresented , comprising less than 3% of the skilled trades. This underrepresentation stems from structural and cultural barriers, including limited recruitment and training opportunities and a male-dominated culture that can be unwelcoming . To address these challenges, the Yelp Foundation is piloting a program in partnership with nonprofit organizations with deep expertise in the services sector. After thorough research, we’ve selected five organizations to fund this year, each tackling challenges in the skilled trades in unique ways: Building Pathways provides pre-apprenticeship workforce training and creates opportunities for low-income and underrepresented populations in the building trades industry. Additionally, Building Pathways has a robust advocacy program, working to support single parents, among other things.  Explore the Trades recruits individuals to plumbing, heating, cooling, and electrical trades. The organization is committed to developing the next generation of skilled workers by changing the perception of the trades starting in high school.  Girls Garage is a design and building program with dedicated workspace for girls and female-identifying youth ages 9–18. Through after-school and summer pathways, Girls Garage provides free and low-cost programs in carpentry, welding, architecture, engineering, and activist art to a diverse community.  NY Helmets to Hardhats is dedicated to the assistance of military veterans as they transition from military duty back to civilian life through careers in union construction. The organization provides the training and connections to secure great union jobs.  TechForce champions all students through their education and into careers as professional technicians with programs that include training from middle school through apprenticeships and access to careers in automotive.  These organizations are breaking down barriers, increasing the supply of skilled workers, and empowering new entrants to secure certifications and training for great jobs and potential business ventures. As part of our trust-based philanthropic approach, we strive to give multi-year funding where possible. So this year, in addition to organizations focused on skilled trades, we are thrilled to be funding the following organizations over the next three years:  826 Valencia supports creative and expository writing skills for underserved youth. Freedom of the Press Foundation’s Press Freedom Tracker documents press freedom violations in the U.S. to protect, defend, and empower public-interest journalists and freedom of speech. Hot Bread Kitchen creates economic opportunity through careers in food by offering culinary training and incubating low-income food entrepreneurs. i.c.stars offers technology-based workforce development and leadership training programs for low-income adults and then connects them with career opportunities. La Cocina cultivates low-income food entrepreneurs as they formalize and grow their businesses. Seed Spot supports impact-driven entrepreneurs in schools and communities. Raising a Reader focuses on early literacy and family engagement for children 0–8 years old. Known for sending children home with little red bags full of books, Raising a Reader has raised more than 1.7 million readers since 1999.  The past year has been transformative for the Yelp Foundation and our nonprofit partners. By concentrating on trades-focused organizations, and continuing to support many of our long-term partners, we’re hoping to make a meaningful difference in the lives of individuals and communities. We are excited to continue this journey and look forward to another year of growth and impact. Brown Friday: Yelp reveals the 20 most clogged cities in the U.S. | Yelp - Official Blog Skip to main content Toggle site navigation Yelp - Official Blog Blog News Businesses Community Life at Yelp Yelp.com Yelp for Business Search Yelp News Brown Friday: Yelp reveals the 20 most clogged cities in the U.S. Spotlighting the top plumbing issues and prevention tips ahead of plumbing’s busiest time of year Tara Lewis VP of Community Expansion + Trends November 20, 2024 Share This As the holiday hosting season approaches, nothing can derail your get-together with loved ones faster than an embarrassing plumbing emergency. From clogged sinks to overflowing toilets, “Brown Friday” — the day following Thanksgiving — is consistently among the plumbing industry’s busiest times of the year. Yelp data revealed that searches for “emergency plumbing” surged 65% during the 2023 Brown Friday time period, when comparing searches from the two weeks before Thanksgiving Day to those on Thanksgiving Day and the two weeks after in 2023. Searches for “24-hour plumbers” were higher on Thanksgiving Day than any other day in November 2023.* With Brown Friday quickly approaching, Yelp is unveiling the top cities facing plumbing predicaments during this time period, along with expert tips on how to holiday-proof your home to help people prepare for guests and find trusted plumbing and service professionals when they need them most. Los Angeles crowned “clogged capital” of the US, followed by Miami  After analyzing millions of data points on Yelp for plumbing-related searches — including clogged toilets, drains, and more — Los Angeles topped the list as the clogged capital of the U.S. The city saw a 73% increase in plumbing searches during the Brown Friday time frame, significantly outpacing any other city on the list. Searches rose sharply in Los Angeles, particularly for services like “plumbing repair” (up 400%), “affordable plumbing” (up 300%), “drain cleaning services” (up 175%), and “emergency plumbing” (up 100%).  Cities from coast to coast experienced the Brown Friday rush. Rounding out the top five cities were Miami (up 37%); Nashville, TN (up 26%); Sacramento, CA (up 24%); and Baltimore (up 23%).** Some cities had more urgent plumbing needs than others, as Yelp regional data shows notable upticks in searches for 24-hour plumbing services. While New York City didn’t break the top clogged cities list, in the city that never sleeps, the plumbing issues don’t end either. During the Brown Friday time period, New York City searches specifically for “24 hour plumber” rose by 64%. “Whether you’re hosting a Thanksgiving feast or game day watch party, plumbing-related emergencies can flush the fun out of any get together fast,” said Tara Lewis, Yelp’s Trend Expert and VP of Community Expansion. “To keep your celebrations on track through Brown Friday and beyond, Yelp can connect you with trusted services professionals who are responsive, reliable, and ready to tackle any plumbing or home issues during the holidays and beyond.” Yelp’s Trend Expert reveals holiday home preparation tips While emergencies can happen, a little prep work can ensure the only thing overflowing in your home this season is holiday joy. Yelp’s Trend Expert Tara Lewis has compiled a list of essential tips to prevent plumbing issues during the busy holiday season and throughout the year. Toss leftovers in the trash, not the sink : To prevent clogs, make sure to scrape food off dishes before placing them in the dishwasher, and use a sink strainer to catch any debris. If you compost, learn what scraps from cooking and baking should be composted versus thrown in the trash. Check for leaks : Before the festivities begin, take a moment to inspect faucets, toilets, and under-sink areas for any signs of leaks. Consider having a professional plumber conduct an inspection to identify potential issues and perform necessary maintenance. Addressing these issues early can save you from bigger headaches later on. Know your shut-off valves : Familiarize yourself with the location of your main water shut-off valve and any local shut-off valves for sinks and toilets. In case of an emergency, you’ll be able to quickly stop the flow of water and minimize damage. Toilet paper only, please! : Put up a friendly sign to remind guests about what can and cannot be flushed. This simple step can help prevent accidental clogs and keep your plumbing system running smoothly. Avoid a kitchen nightmare : Holiday cooking can lead to excess grease and oil, and proper disposal of it is essential. Instead of pouring drippings from your Thanksgiving turkey down the drain, collect grease in a container and dispose of it safely in the trash once it cools and solidifies. Spread out water usage : Try to stagger tasks and allow time between dishwashing, laundry, and showering, to avoid overloading the plumbing system. Check the weather : If freezing temperatures are expected, you can prevent potential pipe issues by allowing faucets to drip slightly. This helps ensure water continues to circulate and reduces the risk of freezing pipes. Find your holiday hero with Yelp’s Request a Quote : Yelp’s Request a Quote feature can help you schedule pre-holiday services or address last-minute issues. Request a Quote allows you to see a service pro’s typical response time, and request and compare quotes from multiple businesses at once, helping you quickly find the right pro during the holiday rush. Find the right pro for every home challenge Plumbing isn’t the only area in the home that can cause issues that dampen holiday cheer. From HVAC specialists to pest control pros and home cleaners , Yelp’s Request a Quote feature can help you find and hire the right service pro for your needs and budget. You can hire with confidence by looking for a business backed by Yelp Guaranteed , a satisfaction-guarantee program that offers you up to $2,500 back in the event something goes wrong with your project when you use Request a Quote, providing you with peace of mind during the process. Not sure where to start? Check out Yelp Assistant , a conversational AI feature that helps efficiently describe your home problem and match you with qualified local businesses for the job.                 Got a question?            

                                                        Is a Yelp Business Page free?                            
Yes. There is no charge to create a Yelp Business Page.

                                                        How do I create a business page on Yelp?                            
Go to 
 biz.yelp.com/claim
 and simply enter your business name to get started.

                                                        How much does it cost to put your business on Yelp?                            
$0. There is no charge for listing your business on Yelp.

                                                        What does it mean to claim a business on Yelp?                            
A “claimed” Business Page is one that has been claimed by the owner or representative of the business through our verification process. Claiming is free, and a claimed page does not mean that the business is a paid advertiser with Yelp.

                                                        How do I promote my business on Yelp?                            
The first step is getting your business on Yelp by creating a free Yelp Business Page. This allows your business to appear in the “organic” search results so you can be found when someone searches for the products, services, and specialties you offer in the geographic area you’re listed in.
Once you have a verified free business page set up, you can promote your products, services, and specialties on your page for free, using your own photos and words. Businesses looking for additional tools to stand out and attract more customers to their page can pay to access the features in the 
Upgrade Package
. Businesses that want to get additional exposure and more leads can choose to promote their business page in the “Sponsored Results” sections with 
Yelp Ads
.

                                                        How long does it take to approve a business?                            
Most new Business Pages are approved and listed on Yelp within 24 hours; however, some pages may take longer to approve if further verification is required by Yelp’s moderation team.

                                                        How do businesses use Yelp?                            
While it varies based on their unique needs, most businesses use Yelp to establish an online presence, manage their reputation, and get new customers so they can grow their business. Yelp created Yelp for Business to provide free self-serve tools that make it easy for businesses to share their photos, hours of operation, services, and other important  information on Yelp. Businesses start by creating a new Business Page, or claiming an existing page via the Yelp for Business app, or by visiting 
 biz.yelp.com/claim
. Once listed on Yelp, they can be found by people searching for their products or services, and give these potential customers the information they need to make a decision. Businesses can update their business information, add new photos, or make other changes to their page 24/7 from their Yelp for Business account. Businesses also have the option to pay to upgrade their page with the Upgrade Package, or drive more leads to their business with Yelp Ads.

                                                        How do I edit my Yelp Page?                            
To edit your page, navigate to the tab labeled “Business Information” from your free Yelp for Business account. You can access your account through the free Yelp for Business app, or log in from 
business.yelp.com
. 

                                                        How can I advertise my business for free?                            
Yelp offers both free and paid products to help promote your business. Our free Yelp Business Page service gets your business listed in organic search results on Yelp at no cost. This business listing page can be found by potential customers as they search on Yelp and gives you access to over 20 free page features that can be used to feature your products, services and specialties on your page. If you want to get additional exposure, our paid product 
Yelp Ads
 enables you to use your advertising budget dollars to appear in the “Sponsored Results” sections on Yelp.

                                                        How will people find my Business Page on Yelp?                            
Potential new customers will be able to find your business on Yelp by searching the categories or keywords related to your business, in your service area or the city where your business is located. Existing customers, or those who know you by name, will be able to find your business by searching for your business name, in your service area or the city where your business is located.

                                                        Will customers be able to contact me from my free Business Page?                            
Yes. There are multiple ways that people can contact you after finding your listing on Yelp. Depending on the information you choose to share for your business, people may call you, visit your website, visit your location, or use Yelp’s free messaging tools to send you a direct message, requesting a quote, consultation or other information.

                                                        I completed the process. Why don’t I see my page live on Yelp?                            
All new businesses go through a review process by Yelp’s moderation team before appearing on Yelp. If you successfully completed the process of claiming your free Business Page (you created a business listing, a Yelp for Business login, and successfully verified your information) and you’re still not seeing your business listed, it may still be in review.

                                                        What are Yelp page upgrades?                            
Page Upgrades is a suite of features that lets you enhance and customize your Yelp Business Page and search listing, so you can quickly show customers why you’re the right one for them. It’s designed to help take someone from simply finding your business to actually choosing your business. You can get a bundle of page upgrades by starting a free trial of the Upgrade Package. Terms apply.
When shown two businesses side-by-side in search, 95% of Yelp users said they’d choose the business with Upgrade Package features over the one without.*
*Based on a survey conducted by Yelp in August 2022. Methodology used ComScore demographics and people who reported having used Yelp in the prior 3 months.

                                                        How much is Yelp’s Upgrade Package?                            
The Upgrade Package is a discounted bundle of features (up to 7 based on eligibility) to help you tell your story and get chosen on Yelp. The standard price of the feature bundle is $6 per day on average. We offer a 14 day free trial, so you can try it risk free. Terms apply. You can cancel anytime if you choose the daily pricing option. 

                                                        What is an Enhanced Profile on Yelp?                            
The Enhanced Profile is a legacy bundle that includes a small portion of available Page Upgrades (Call to Action, Removing Competitors Ads and Slideshow). The Upgrade Package has replaced the Enhanced Profile for new local businesses joining Yelp, as it includes everything in the Enhanced Profile, as well as newly built Page Upgrade features. If you have Enhanced Profile and would like to change to the Upgrade Package, contact 
(877) 767-9357
.

                                                        What is Yelp slideshow?                            
Slideshow is one of the features included in the Upgrade Package to help you make a great first impression. It lets you choose the order of the photo displayed on your Yelp search listing and your Business Page.

                                                        How is the Upgrade Package different from Yelp Ads?                            
Yelp Ads
 helps your business reach 2.5x more leads* by putting you on primary placements on Yelp, such as above the search results and on your competitors’ pages.
The Upgrade Package lets you enhance and customize your Yelp Business Page and search listing, so you can quickly show customers that you’re the right one for them.
Yelp Ads and the Upgrade Package are designed to compliment each other. One gets your business in front of more customers, one helps you attract and get chosen by the right customers.

                Frequently Asked Questions            

                                                        What is the difference between Yelp Fusion and Yelp Fusion Insights?                            
Both products provide API Access to Yelp’s core dataset. 
Yelp Fusion is designed for consumer-facing products, displaying Yelp search and business data on third-party apps, platforms and websites.  
Yelp Fusion Insights serves business-to-business (B2B) use cases, providing location data and web traffic analytics for internal, non-public/back-end purposes such as internal analysis.  There are no display rights associated with a Yelp Fusion Insights license.

                                                        What types of business attributes can I access through the Yelp Fusion Insights API?                            
The API provides over 230 attributes for businesses and points of interest (POI) to reviews and web traffic analytics.

                                                        What consumer engagement insights are available through the Yelp Fusion Insights API?                            
Our Premium plan offers consumer engagement metrics including search appearances/impressions and a consumer engagement score, which can help assess the level of interaction with a business on Yelp.  Get in touch with a Yelp rep to learn more.

                                                        Can the Yelp Fusion Insights API help identify new and emerging businesses in a location?                            
Yes, it provides insights into look-alike businesses, those opening soon, newly-opened businesses and when a business was last updated.

                                                        What food and drink insights can I obtain from the Yelp Fusion Insights API?                            
The API provides extracted meta data on dishes and drinks offered, popular items and raw food ingredients for businesses.

                                                        Is it possible to compare businesses using the Yelp Fusion Insights API?                            
Yes, the Fusion Insights API offers local and competitive insights, allowing for comparisons between similar businesses in a given area.

                        How electrician Matt Mark gets up to 70% of his clients by advertising on Yelp                    
I advertised with Yelp and was amazed with the results.
— Steve H., Owner, 
Matt Mark Service Company
, and Yelp advertiser, Kansas City, MO
Steve recommends:
Yelp Ads
 | 
Business analytics

            Video transcript        
I became an electrician in 1972. Ever since I started my business, I've always been home-based. I perform all my own functions, and this home-based business has worked well.

                Read More            
I have had people ask me what I would recommend in advertising, and I said, you talked to the right person because I’ve tried everything. I have tried sponsoring bowling teams, little league baseball teams. I figured, I said, I sponsor the little league baseball team, maybe mom and dad will need some work. I think I got two jobs three years later from one of the moms and dads, but I found that if you just get into a search engine optimization program, and I’m hounded by them every day: ‘We got a better program. We can do your website better.’ You’re really taking a chance. So I feel comfortable with Yelp because they’ve been around. I would say that the business that I got before I started advertising with Yelp, it was 10%, and then I advertised with Yelp truly on a whim, and I was amazed at the results.
I’ve been around long enough that I used to think Yellow Pages was the greatest thing in the world, and at the time it was because that’s all that was available. But this has surpassed it so much. My personal exposure right now is greater than it ever was three years ago, and there are some months when I would say that 70% of the business comes from Yelp. So it’s really great that after looking all these years that I actually literally stumbled into something that is working well. And if it’s not broke, I’m not going to fix it.

                        How Morgan Miller Plumbing achieved a 10:1 ROI with Yelp Ads                    
I know my ROI from Yelp is going to be there month after month.
— Jeff M., Owner, 
Morgan Miller Plumbing
, and Yelp advertiser, Grandview, MO
Jeff recommends:
Yelp Ads
 | 
Call to Action button

            Video transcript        
My name's Jeff Morgan. I'm the son of a son of a plumber. I've had my own plumbing company for 18 years. Four years ago, our business consisted of word-of-mouth advertising. There was eight to 10 people. Today we've doubled that and plan on doubling it again in the next four years and maybe less.

                Read More            
We stumbled upon Yelp three years ago. We already knew Yelp was working because we had reviews on Yelp. We didn’t even know what it was at the time. So when we talked to our account manager, who called us and informed us of these reviews, it was a very short amount of time before we decided to jump in, and it was scary at first. It was cutting-edge technology. It was nowhere where we’d ever spent any advertising dollars before, so it was new and it’s always scary for an old guy.
I will tell you, as a business owner, I like Yelp best because right off the bat, we were informed that we could only pay them the amount that they had for traffic. There’s only 200 people a month looking at their website for a plumbing company. They’re only going to be able to charge us X amount of months for advertising, otherwise, we’re just giving them money for nothing. As Yelp has expanded and more people are on Yelp, then our advertising dollars can go up. That made a big difference to us. That made us trust Yelp right away.
Every month, I’ve really dug in to see where each and every dollar came from. It’s about a 10-to-one return. It’s been very consistent, and that’s the beautiful thing about today, is that you get this instant feedback. I’m not sitting there hoping that my Yellow Pages had worked this year. I know my ROI is going to be there month after month. It’s easy.

My name is Ryan. I’m with Tempoe Entertainment DJs. We’re one of the highest-rated DJ companies in the area on Yelp. We’ve been in business for over 17 years.
